status: provisional bars from lab/TARGETS.md section 1; calibration may tighten, loosening needs Sam
population: SCALE_POPULATION year-one (obligations.json scalePopulation), on one identified profile and composition

writerTrace.source: lab/TARGETS.md section 2 (fixed workload, from Sam's paste)

commandShape.documents: a blob reference for document commands

readsPerWrite.what: each command triggers a reconcile pull at the returned tx, dependency lookups, projection updates and UI refreshes

writerTrace.conflicts: optimistic compare-and-set on the subject's last position; serial per subject, parallel across subjects
writerTrace.bulkLane: separate and throttled; used only by the bulk measurements
writerTrace.seeded: a recorded seed fixes the whole trace; the same seed gives the same bytes

subjectChoice.activeSetDistribution: Zipf s = 1.1 over a seeded ranking

generator.commandSize: uniform within each band of the 60/30/10 mix
generator.offers: open loop: a seeded Poisson process at the steady rate
generator.burstPhase: bursts start at 120 s + k x 600 s from the start of the measured window, identical for baselines and candidates
generator.scenarioOverlay: a golden scenario's commands are added on top of the background trace, never instead of it; both streams accounted separately in the receipt
generator.freeze: the generator source hash and the seed are bound in every receipt; a change to either starts a new comparison series

frozenScreening.rule: each screening series has its own frozen entry, frozen by EXP-M01 (RULINGS Q64b, Q60g, Q69f); frozen is the acceptance trace; until frozen, claims stay diagnostics

frozen.rule: a required input: the generator source sha256, the seed and the offer schedule's sha256, pinned by a contract version once the trace is frozen; while null no CR-NS or CR-GS comparison has a workload identity and every such claim is a diagnostic (RULINGS Q61h)

invalidCommands.rule: 0.1% of trace commands are deliberately invalid (values no engine may hold) and marked in the frozen trace; only those may end in a typed rejection

Q74a.rule: Screening and development receipts may be seeded by clone of a golden; the receipt records `seededBy: clone` with the golden key (adapter commit, world and seed-generator hash, driver seed options, image digest, engine config hash) and the golden's freeze fingerprint. Acceptance runs seed fresh (TARGETS 6).

Q74b.rule: becomes the **recipe**: two finish-blocks, jobs-0 waits, `docker stop -t 60`, copy from a stopped container. A timeout refuses; nothing in it grants.

Q74c.rule: No clone-seeded receipt counts, even for screening, until validation E1 passes: a fresh-seeded slot against its clone under the PAIR-0 A/A procedure, holding within 1.10 at p50 and 1.15 at p99, with R26 section 6.9's seven predictions checked. **unchanged**; E1 is rerun when the recipe, the image or the XTDB version changes

Q74d.rule: **replaced** by Q93a/b: health precondition plus G0 in the driver; `owner.json` holds slot ownership only

Q74e.rule: Runs that measure P1 force one `finish-block` at a fixed trace time in every window, on every arm, so a settled clone still has a maintenance event.

Q74f.rule: A golden or clone is made only when host free disk after the copy stays at or above 5 GiB; clone volumes are removed after each run. At the 10k rung (3.41 GiB per XTDB volume) that allows one clone at a time today.

Q74g.rule: A broker composition clones the engine volume and the broker directory together, from one stopped moment.

Q83a.rule: **kept as a diagnostic aid**; no rule requires the lines

Q83b.rule: **superseded by Q93a**: the steps stay in the recipe, their readings become diagnostics; `xt.live_tables` is read only on a freshly started node (K3)

Q83c.rule: kept for diagnostic tools; B never reads `xt.block_files`

Q93a.rule: For seed reuse on every lane, the only evidence that grants admission is a content fingerprint (G0) read through the engine by the process that will measure, on the endpoint it measures, before its warm-up, compared with a digest pinned before the freeze began (and with O-DOMAIN where one exists). Every other observation (stop, settle, log tails, frontiers, inspect, stderr, timers, owner state, copy hashes, plan hashes, disk) is refusal-only or a diagnostic, and no decision reads a diagnostic.

Q93b.rule: Fields, pinning point and counts as in sections 2.1 and 3.2; every read has a deadline; the golden is published only after two starts of a clone each reproduce `D` and the layout digest `L`.

Q93c.rule: G0 admits a clone by the full digest D over every stored column (byte-level identity with its golden). E1, which compares a clone with a fresh seed of the same inputs, uses a second digest D' over the same columns with engine-assigned values normalized: engine-generated ids and system timestamps are replaced by their rank in commit order, and every other column is kept as is. A fresh seed must match the golden's D', never its D. The normalization list is part of the G0 module, each entry with a comment naming the engine source that assigns it, and a test fails if a column is normalized without one.

freezeProtocol.grant: G0 content fingerprint only; read in the measuring process on its measured endpoint before warm-up every run
freezeProtocol.pinBefore: after last seed commit, before first finish-block
freezeProtocol.cloneDigest: D: every stored column, byte-level identity to golden
freezeProtocol.freshSeedDigest: D-prime: same columns; only engine-assigned ids/system timestamps normalized to rank in commit order; every normalization has an engine-source comment and a test
freezeProtocol.scope: all seed-scope assertions (all value/lifetime columns), claims, attempts; tx_meta enumerates every scope
freezeProtocol.counts: independent COUNT(*) equals closed-form manifest counts; tx_meta holds only the seed scope; W0 worlds and R2 outputs equal O-DOMAIN
freezeProtocol.deadlines: every read has a deadline; timeout refuses
freezeProtocol.goldenPublication: two starts of a qualification clone each reproduce D and L before golden publication
refusalOnly: started-node quiescence: jobs 0 over three readings, live rows 0, layout L, transaction T, lag 0
end counts start plus recorded commands
freezeProtocol.ownerJson: slot ownership only; no readiness admission
freezeProtocol.blockListing: diagnostic tools only; B never reads xt.block_files
freezeProtocol.e1: fresh D-prime equals golden D-prime; PAIR-0 A/A p50 <= 1.10 and p99 <= 1.15; rerun on recipe/image/XTDB version changes

qleverEvidencePolicy.phase0: copy on exclusive slot, never shared resident
qleverEvidencePolicy.phase1: 10M-triple base; scan/join versus delta, monotonic and spread keys
qleverEvidencePolicy.phase2: blue/green generations rebuilt from broker log; leases bind every multi-request read to one generation; Q89i byte identity across every swap

goldenScenarioPolicy.world: W0-valid; domain claims checked by O-DOMAIN or fail closed; W01 retired
goldenScenarioPolicy.background: frozen TARGETS 2.1 trace via W0 mapper; private writerTrace retired
goldenScenarioPolicy.GS04b: required exactly when a separate current store exists
goldenScenarioPolicy.GS04: engine-kill schedule every lane, exclusive only
goldenScenarioPolicy.outbox: product atomic outbox for GS.10 and GS.19; harness file only diagnostic P3 checks
goldenScenarioPolicy.GS10: round C after A/B race required for closure
goldenScenarioPolicy.GS03: W0-1.2 signal-ack pending implementation; superseded outcome flagged for Sam

Q96a.rule: P2 is measured per subject serially and in parallel across subjects, with the queue inside the candidate (Q51a); A0's single-flight composition stays only as a control arm. Golden scenario commit bars measured on single-flight A0 are DIAGNOSTIC (they measure queueing).

Q96b.rule: RT01 round A's client stamp is monotone only because A0 serializes every commit; any per-subject concurrent arm uses a decider-side stamp (the engine stamp after probe p9, or the broker's), per Q90c. RT01 round A's added scope-wide scan on A0 is measured on an engine before RT01 merges (G6).

Q96c.topic: the shortest path and the native check
Q96c.rule: Lane X's shortest path to P2 is XTDB behind the broker (EXP-P2B, Q51b, Q58b). EXP-P2X2 (lab/experiments/EXP-P2X2/BRIEF.md) runs once on an exclusive xtdb-s1 slot after K01's live run and before P5 A1, to settle whether the native path is closed, with the decision rule written in R39 4.5 before the run (native is closed if F3 p50 > 6 ms, or F5 p50 > 20 ms, or engine resolve > 7 ms per commit). If closed, the lab says so plainly (SCOPE 3.2) and keeps the native arm as a comparison.

Q96d.topic: native lane X P2 is closed
Q96d.rule: EXP-P2X2 (exp/P2X2-commit-floor b9a76c0, one exclusive xtdb-s1 run) met Q96c's preregistered rule: F3 p50 7.68 ms (bar 6) and F5 fresh 33.00 ms (bar 20). The XTDB-native commit path cannot meet P2 in this VM, which the lab states plainly (SCOPE 3.2); lane X's P2 candidate is XTDB behind the broker (EXP-P2B), and the native per-subject arm stays as a comparison. Aged F6, F7 to F9 and strict no-wait checks remain open as diagnostics, and the run awaits an independent review of its receipts.

Q97a.rule: Lane Q serves current-value pulls from the broker's SQLite H1 store, behind a default-off currentRoute: "h1" option; QLever keeps history, native SPARQL and analytics. This is the ruled design (Q68a, Q50a, Q68d), which SQL01 used only as an outage fallback. A route that cannot answer a basis exactly refuses (Q89b, Q89c, Q92h). EXP-QH1 (lab/experiments/EXP-QH1/BRIEF.md) builds it after P2Q and SQL01 merge; its G1 to G7 need no slot, G8 takes one exclusive qlever-s1 run.

Q97b.rule: Every QLever latency measured from the host through QleverClient so far carries a 41 to 45 ms keep-alive stall on about a third of requests, because QLever never sets TCP_NODELAY and QleverClient keeps connections alive. QLever latency receipts record the connection mode; earlier QLever latency numbers are DIAGNOSTIC on this ground too. The fix is measured first as a connection per request from the host (no custom image), with the engine patch as the fallback.

Q97c.rule: A pull form that needs one request per BFS level cannot meet P4 from the host on QLever (transport alone is 18 to 32 ms per depth-6 pull), so no multi-request QLever pull form is a P4 candidate.

perSurface: P1, P4 and P5 run separately in each lane language (xtdb-xtql, xtdb-sql, qlever-sparql, datomic-datalog query and pull); P2 and P3 run per engine; a mixed-language run is a diagnostic only

P1.readers: closed-loop, zero think time, each reader a distinct client id
P1.zeroReaderBaseline: level 0 = writer trace alone, same trace segment and burst phase
P1.readShape: subject pull (P4 shape) at a named basis: valid time plus record time or tx; 80% at the latest committed tx (named exactly), 15% at a tx within the last hour, 5% at a past basis up to 90 days back (RULINGS Q16, TARGETS section 2)
P1.hostServedReads: provisional: reads served from the broker count for the P1 and P4 bars when the receipt records route = host and the per-core denominator includes broker and kernel CPU (RULINGS Q68d)

hotSet.rule: at least 50% of reads target subjects written in the previous 60 s (the writer trace's active set)

splitReads.rule: 10% of subgraph reads are issued as two or more queries at the same named basis, scheduled to straddle a command the frozen trace already holds for that subject: step 1 before that command's ACK, step 2 after it; the answer must equal the oracle at the requested basis, never the latest state
splitReads.driverWrites: none: the driver adds no writes of its own, so faster readers never change the write load (RULINGS Q31b)

P1.maintenance: every P1 window contains at least one maintenance event (XTDB compaction; QLever index rebuild or delta merge; index-layer catch-up)
P1.requestedBasis: the driver records the basis it requested (from the receipts it observed) independently of anything the engine echoes; the verifier checks every sampled answer at the driver-recorded basis
writerWaitAttribution: writer latency at each reader level against the zero-reader run on the same trace segment and burst phase
engine-side wait evidence where exposed (QLever broker queue wait); XTDB has no read-path locks, so its evidence is the matched-phase comparison
record: writer commit latency p50, p99, max and throughput per level
P1.recovery: after the 1,024 window, readers return to 256; 30 s evaluation windows sliding by 5 s; recovery time = end of the first window meeting every 256-level bar; must be within NS-P1-RECOVERY-MS

P2.loop: open loop on the frozen offer schedule (WRITER_TRACE generator)
P2.latency: from the scheduled offer time to the published ACK (sent only after the commit is durable and readable), so queueing behind other writers counts
P2.commands: the trace's own commands; the 10-fact probe is a diagnostic only
P2.readGuarantees: each serving surface the composition claims is measured against COMPOSITION readGuarantees (RULINGS Q55c, provisional)
P2.hotSubjects: COMPOSITION hotSubjects; E-OVERLOADED counts as an unjustified outcome (RULINGS Q51a)
P2.storagePerCommit: reported, never a bar: bytes and triples per 10-fact command on both lanes (EXP-J01; XTDB A0 27,581 bytes against the candidate's 95,364; QLever A0 653 triples per 10-fact command as V-P2Q measured it: 24 rows (10 facts and 14 journal rows) of about 27 triples each, the candidate 655 plus a 4-triple deleted marker, against R17's 94; the cause is the row encoding and journal on every lane, not the broker (RULINGS Q62c)), plus xt.txs and METADATA cost at 1M+ transactions (RULINGS Q50c, Q51d, Q51f)
P2.accounting: every offered command is committed with a receipt, rejected with a typed error, or a typed conflict; zero unaccounted (NS-P2-UNACCOUNTED-MAX)

progress.rule: every oracle-valid trace command publishes; typed rejections count only for commands the frozen trace marks deliberately invalid, typed conflicts only where the oracle independently finds a compare-and-set race (NS-P2-UNJUSTIFIED-OUTCOMES-MAX)
progress.queueBound: queued commands never exceed NS-P2-QUEUE-MAX-S of the offered rate at steady state
progress.burstDrain: the queue drains within NS-P2-BURST-DRAIN-S after each burst

P2.ryow: the next pull at the returned tx
P2.idempotency: the trace's duplicates and lost ACKs

runQueue.qleverExclusiveFirst: A0 and candidate at delta 0, 100k and 500k; persist-updates off; kill -9 replay; rebuild trigger cost; the full trace with burst against QLever; a keep-alive recheck on an idle slot (RULINGS Q50e)
runQueue.xtdb100kRung: deferred until EXP-J01 lands; the disk need is re-estimated from the new bytes per commit before a large slot is requested (RULINGS Q51e)

P3.commitTime: the source's own publication timestamp for each position (the broker's durable watermark update, or the engine's commit resolution when the engine is the source), stamped by the source on the host monotonic clock the driver also reads, recorded independently of ACK delivery (RULINGS Q55d)
P3.accounting: every committed position is accounted; no lag sample is dropped for a missing ACK; a position with no consumer record is counted and fails the run (RULINGS Q55d)
P3.publicationEnumeration: both arms enumerate the final published source prefix from the source's own record and timestamp actual publication (broker: watermark publication; engine as source: commit resolution); ACK records are reconciled afterwards; a late or lost ACK is never a feed defect (RULINGS Q67d)
P3.cursor: (epoch, position), a total order over transactions; per-subject order follows from it
P3.expectedAffected: subjects written directly (O-REPLAY) plus the subjects whose WORLD_W0 static read set contains a changed fact (O-DOMAIN; RULINGS Q36e)
P3.milestone: the consumer durably records the affected-subject set and its checkpoint in one durable write; lag runs from commit time to that record
P3.delivery: at-least-once from the last checkpoint; effects keyed by (consumer, position, subject), so replay is idempotent; visible duplicate effects must be zero (NS-P3-VISIBLE-DUP-EFFECTS-MAX); replay attempts allowed and counted separately
crashPoints: after the effect, before the checkpoint

P4.probe: single client, subject pulls at the current basis
P4.tails: the p50 and p99 bars apply to the weighted mix; each bucket reports its own p50 and p99; the largest bucket has NS-P4-PULL-P99-LARGEST-MS
P4.throughput: closed-loop pulls; cores = the CPU quota bound in the receipt; host broker and kernel CPU reported beside engine-core throughput
P4.history: one matched sample of 1,000 subjects: measure at history depth 1, add corrections to the same subjects to depth 3 and then 10, measure again; compare p99 latency and bytes read (RULINGS Q16, Q27)
P4.hostServedReads: provisional: reads served from the broker count for the P4 bars when the receipt records route = host and the per-core denominator includes broker and kernel CPU (RULINGS Q68d)

P5.sweep: evaluate release R against WORLD_W0 for every subject in R's scope (100k) at one shared basis; the receipt binds the basis and R's content hash
P5.coverage: every in-scope subject evaluated exactly once; the receipt carries the hash of the subject list

scopedRelease.binds: the reached-subject list and its sha256, instead of every placement
scopedRelease.why: R3 is vacuous above the 100k rung (V-D01 N3); a scoped sweep's receipt binds what it reached (V-D01 N4; RULINGS Q48b)

P5.publication: results published as work items through the atomic outbox path (EP-OUTBOX) under the delivery key (id, publication sequence) with early cutoff: a payload equal to the latest published one publishes nothing, a different one (including a return to an earlier payload) publishes the next sequence of the same id; publication state is persisted atomically with the outbox record (RULINGS Q36a, Q38f); expected outputs from O-DOMAIN, independently
P5.postCaptureMutations: after the basis is captured the driver mutates selected subjects; their outputs must reflect the captured basis
P5.throttledVariant: about 10 minutes, overlapping a real compaction or index rebuild; keeps its basis and never blocks writers
P5.concurrent: the writer trace and 64 live readers
P5.noSweepBaseline: same run, same 64 readers and writer trace, before the sweep

secondary.bulk: a 1M-fact import through the bulk lane with 64 live readers; bar NS-SEC-BULK-READ-P99-RATIO
secondary.retroactive: 1,000 corrections 30 days back; feed valid-time range and explain at the old basis checked
secondary.audit: explain at a past basis, repeated three times; bit-for-bit identical

measurementProtocol.status: PROVISIONAL (RULINGS Q60); the margins are the orchestrator's interpretation and adjustable (NORTH-STAR item 4)

design.rule: comparisons run as paired rounds: a duet (A0 and candidate at the same time on two identically configured slots, same trace window) or, as the fallback, same-engine ABBA; a single run never decides a bar (RULINGS Q60a)
design.statistic: pooled-quantile ratios with a bootstrap over rounds
design.aa: A/A rounds in the pre-flight and every sixth round

margins.superiority: the lower bound of A/B at or above the claimed ratio (1.25 by default)
margins.hold: the upper bound of B/A at or below 1.10 for p50 and 1.15 for p99

slotRegime.rule: measurement slots run with a cpuset and no CPU quota; receipts record the effective cpu.max, cpuset and cpu.weight; quota and cpuset arms are never compared; A0 is measured again under the new regime (RULINGS Q60c)

measurementProtocol.accounting: latency histograms include every offered command (expired, failed and rejected ones at their censor time) next to the committed-only view; reads get an open-loop probe at a fixed rate; per-second goodput and per-second maximum latency are recorded (RULINGS Q60d)
measurementProtocol.windows: absolute bars are judged only in GREEN windows (the pre-registered noise signals and the A/A gate of R22 section 4.2); outside them an absolute bar is reported unjudged, which never counts as met (RULINGS Q60e)

screeningSeries.rule: a screening trace with a burst every 180 s is a new comparison series (TARGETS 2.1 item 5), so P2 and P3 rounds contain enough commands for p99; acceptance keeps the frozen trace (RULINGS Q60g)

fallback.name: screening-r4
fallback.rule: 4x the steady rate, no bursts; pre-registered and used only if the burst series makes commitAll p50 NOT_ESTIMABLE in the A/A run (RULINGS Q69f)

measurementProtocol.lease: a measurement window takes every heavy token and freezes pool admission for its duration (RULINGS Q60h)
measurementProtocol.a0: EXP-N01's single-run A0 is diagnostic only; A0 numbers for comparisons come from paired rounds (RULINGS Q60i)
measurementProtocol.windowProcedure: the pool cannot hold two 3.5 GiB slots beside both dev residents, so a measurement window stops one dev resident for its duration (qlever-dev by default, recreated fresh after; xtdb-dev when the window is QLever's) once no running agent depends on it; the orchestrator announces the window in STATE; no agent starts engine work during it; the lease enforces it (RULINGS Q69a)

verdicts.INVALID: a protocol departure: development overrides, the wrong regime, no lease, or an unregistered round count
verdicts.INVALID_NOISE: a window that fails the noise gate

measurementProtocol.aaInAbMode: provisional: A/B windows grade from the all-round s_d (conservative); acceptance-level claims add a second pair of container lifetimes with roles swapped (RULINGS Q69c)
measurementProtocol.continuousTrace: duets run one continuous trace, so both arms see the same content at the same time; ABBA fallback runs keep per-round window randomization (RULINGS Q69d)
measurementProtocol.liveComposition: the live A/A uses public-queued, matching EXP-N01's A0 (RULINGS Q69e)
measurementProtocol.calibration: thresholds stay as pre-registered; a passive recorder (signals every 10 s, calibration every 10 minutes) runs for 7 days to set them, started after EXP-M01 merges (RULINGS Q69g)

windows.judging: absolute bars are judged only in GREEN windows (the pre-registered noise signals and the A/A gate of R22 section 4.2); outside them an absolute bar is reported unjudged, which never counts as met (RULINGS Q60e)

acceptance.note: RULINGS Q16; 600 s covers one full burst cycle of the writer trace (60 s at 750 facts/s every 600 s)

screening.note: RULINGS Q16; candidate comparison only; a screening receipt never closes an obligation

basisMix.basis: a tx within the last hour
a past basis up to 90 days back

semantics: lab/TARGETS.md section 1.1 (frozen before any comparison): a run that departs from these definitions cannot close an NS obligation
invariants: every read names its basis and its answer is compared with the oracle at the driver-recorded requested basis; a wrong answer scores zero
receipts bind the composition, the trace generator hash and seed, and the serving index's watermark at every read (VA14, VA15)
every command gets one receipt; duplicates and lost ACKs return the original receipt (COMMIT_OUTCOMES)
no engine restart, crash or OOM inside a measurement window unless the scenario injects it

NS-P1-VIOLATIONS-MAX.unit: correctness violations at every reader level

NS-P1-GOODPUT-256-VS-64.unit: correctness-qualified read goodput at 256 readers divided by goodput at 64 readers
NS-P1-GOODPUT-256-VS-64.source: lab/TARGETS.md section 1 P1 (goodput does not fall from the 64-reader level)

NS-P1-WRITER-P99-RATIO-256.unit: writer commit p99 at 256 readers divided by its zero-reader baseline in the same run

NS-P1-WRITER-WAIT-MAX-MS.unit: ms, no command waits longer (every ladder level)

NS-P1-GOODPUT-1024-VS-256.unit: read goodput at 1,024 readers divided by the 256 level

NS-P1-WRITER-P99-RATIO-1024.unit: writer commit p99 at 1,024 readers divided by the zero-reader baseline

NS-P1-RECOVERY-MS.unit: ms after stress until an evaluation window meets every 256-level P1 bar

NS-P2-COMMIT-P50-MS.unit: ms commit p50 from scheduled offer to published ACK, applied separately to the trace commands of the 5-to-10 and 11-to-25 fact bands, 256 readers running
NS-P2-COMMIT-P50-MS.source: lab/TARGETS.md section 1 P2; TARGETS 1.1 P2 items 1 and 2

NS-P2-COMMIT-P99-MS.unit: ms commit p99 from scheduled offer to published ACK, applied separately to the 5-to-10 and 11-to-25 fact bands, 256 readers running
NS-P2-COMMIT-P99-MS.source: lab/TARGETS.md section 1 P2; TARGETS 1.1 P2 items 1 and 2

NS-P2-COMMIT-P99-26-50-MS.unit: ms commit p99 from scheduled offer to published ACK for the 26-to-50 fact band (provisional)

NS-P2-UNACCOUNTED-MAX.unit: offered commands with no receipt, typed error or typed conflict

NS-P2-UNJUSTIFIED-OUTCOMES-MAX.unit: oracle-valid trace commands that did not publish: typed rejections of commands the trace did not mark invalid, plus typed conflicts where the oracle finds no compare-and-set race

NS-P2-QUEUE-MAX-S.unit: s of the offered rate: queued (offered, not yet published) commands at any steady-state instant, divided by the steady offered rate

NS-P2-BURST-DRAIN-S.unit: s after each burst ends until the queue is back within NS-P2-QUEUE-MAX-S

NS-P2-RYOW-FRACTION.unit: fraction of pulls at the returned tx that see the commit with no extra wait

NS-P2-DUP-RECEIPT-FRACTION.unit: fraction of duplicates and lost-ACK retries that return the original receipt

NS-P3-LAG-P99-MS.unit: ms p99 from commit time (the source's publication instant on the shared host monotonic clock) to the consumer's single durable write of the affected-subject set and its checkpoint, 256 readers running
NS-P3-LAG-P99-MS.source: lab/TARGETS.md section 1 P3; TARGETS 1.1 P3 items 1 and 4

NS-P3-VISIBLE-DUP-EFFECTS-MAX.unit: externally visible duplicate consumer effects per run (replay attempts are counted separately and allowed)

NS-P4-PULL-P50-MS.unit: ms single-client subject pull p50 at the current basis over the frozen weighted bucket mix
NS-P4-PULL-P50-MS.source: lab/TARGETS.md section 1 P4; TARGETS 1.1 P4 item 1

NS-P4-PULL-P99-MS.unit: ms single-client subject pull p99 over the frozen weighted bucket mix
NS-P4-PULL-P99-MS.source: lab/TARGETS.md section 1 P4; TARGETS 1.1 P4 item 1

NS-P4-PULL-P99-LARGEST-MS.unit: ms pull p99 of the largest bucket (801 to 2,000 facts), provisional

NS-P4-PULLS-PER-CORE.unit: pulls/s per engine core, cores = the CPU quota bound in the receipt; host broker and kernel CPU reported beside it
NS-P4-PULLS-PER-CORE.source: lab/TARGETS.md section 1 P4; TARGETS 1.1 P4 item 3

NS-P4-HISTORY-FLATNESS.unit: current-pull p99 latency and bytes read at history depth 10 divided by depth 1, on one matched sample of 1,000 subjects grown from depth 1 to 3 to 10
NS-P4-HISTORY-FLATNESS.source: RULINGS Q16, Q27; lab/TARGETS.md 1.1 P4 item 2

NS-P5-SWEEP-S.unit: s wall time for the release sweep: W0 evaluation of release R for 100k in-scope subjects at one shared basis, including outbox publication
NS-P5-SWEEP-S.source: lab/TARGETS.md section 1 P5; TARGETS 1.1 P5 items 1 and 5

NS-P5-LIVE-READ-P99-RATIO.unit: live read p99 during the sweep divided by no-sweep

NS-P5-WRITER-P99-RATIO.unit: writer commit p99 during the sweep divided by no-sweep

NS-SEC-BULK-READ-P99-RATIO.unit: live read p99 during a 1M-fact bulk import divided by without

calibration.rule: Calibration may only tighten a threshold (a smaller max, a larger min) or record it UNATTAINABLE with the measurement. Loosening any value needs Sam (TARGETS threshold policy); until he rules, the obligation stays OPEN.
procedure: C1 preconditions: S.population.year-one closed (VA) on the control profile; this file's sha256 recorded
C2 run every measurement once per lane on the control profile with the fixed writer trace
C3 for each NS bar, record the measured value; keep the bar, tighten it, or mark UNATTAINABLE with the measurement (loosening needs Sam)
C4 write the create-only calibration record (VC); acceptance runs cite it
